name: Refund voucher
definition: A refund voucher is issued under clause (e) of section 31(3) when an advance is refunded and no supply is made. Rule 51 fixes eleven particulars, (a) to (k), and clause (e) requires it to name the receipt voucher it reverses.
why_it_exists: It closes an advance that never became a supply. Clause (e) makes the link explicit, which is what lets a refund be matched to the receipt it undoes instead of floating as an unexplained payment out.
outputs: the set of rule 51 particulars found
the set of mandatory particulars absent
preconditions: an advance previously recorded on a receipt voucher is being refunded
exceptions: rule 54(5) extends the rule 54(2) and 54(4) relaxations to refund vouchers
common_mistakes: treating a refund voucher as a credit note — a credit note under section 34 adjusts a supply already invoiced; a refund voucher undoes an advance where no supply happened
accepting a refund voucher with no reference to the receipt voucher — clause (e) requires the number and date
legal_references: UNKNOWN — clause (e) of sub-section (3) of section 31 of the CGST Act was not read for this record
gst_references: UNKNOWN — source is the Rules as at 01-01-2022; later amendments not held locally
evidence_required: the referenced receipt voucher number and date
confidence_factors: weak when the referenced receipt voucher cannot be located, because the reversal cannot then be matched
validation_checks: all eleven particulars (a) to (k) are present
clause (e) names a receipt voucher issued under rule 50
the referenced receipt voucher exists in the books
examples: a voucher naming receipt voucher RV-118 dated 4 May, refunding the advance and the tax on it
counterexamples: a voucher with no receipt voucher reference — clause (e) fails

evidence.quote: 51. Refund voucher.-A refund voucher referred to in clause (e) of sub-section (3) of section 31 shall contain the following particulars, namely:-
number and date of receipt voucher issued in accordance with the provisions of rule 50;
